preamble: Backing and rounding of [i] to [u] is rare as a regular change but occurs as a conditioned assimilation next to labials, especially after [w]. In Old English, early widu 'wood' and widuwe 'widow' developed variants wudu and wuduwe, where the rounded labial-velar glide [w] spread its rounding and backness to the following high vowel; wudu became the standard form and survives as Modern English wood.

examples.note: Assimilated after w; wudu, also spelled wudo, is the usual later form, already written runically ᚹᚢᛞᚢ on the Franks Casket.
West Saxon variant with the same rounding after w.

sources: Campbell, A. (1959). Old English Grammar. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
